title: Reliability orchestration action grid and sprint notes
summary: Working notes and an actionable grid for orchestrating SLO ownership, automated fallbacks, and cross-team sprint work. This is an experimental playbook to reduce drift between product SLO intent and operational implementation.
objectives:
- Make SLO implementation repeatable across feature teams
- Reduce time-to-detection for customer-impacting SLO regressions by 40% in 90 days
- Codify automated fallback patterns (model variant routing, cache bypass, degrade-to-minimal-path)
- Establish a small catalogue of runbook snippets that feature teams can reuse
scope: Covers: text-generation endpoints, chat routes, and embeddings routes in hosted and dedicated deployments. Excludes: private on-prem packaging, billing pipelines, and infra provisioning tasks that require infra-ownership signoff.
audience_and_stakeholders: Primary: SRE (ops), Serving runtime, Platform eng, Product-hosted-api, Solutions eng. Secondary: Customer success, Security. Stakeholder owners assigned in the action grid below.
orchestration_action_grid:
Columns: SLO type | Customer impact example | Primary owner | Observable signals | Detection query | Runbook snippet | Automated action | Escalation path | Sprint ticket template

1) Availability (5xx rate / success rate) | outbound API 5xx spike for chat: customers time out | Owner: SRE-service-bridge | Signals: 5xx-rate, latency-p50/p95, pod restarts, gpu-utilization | Detection: 1m query: sum(rate(http_server_errors[1m]))/sum(rate(http_requests[1m])) > 0.03 and p95_latency>1s | Runbook snippet: check model-pool health -> verify routing -> toggle fallback model variant -> notify on-call -> open incident if persists 5m 
Automated action: circuit-breaker to fallback model variant + route to warm standby pool.
Escalation: on-call -> SRE triage -> Serving runtime lead if model variant failing.
Sprint ticket template: SRE-ops: investigate 5xx root cause; add canary; add fallback test.

2) Latency (p95/p99 token latency) | p99 token time increases during long-context requests | Owner: serving-runtime | Signals: kv-cache-hit-rate, batch size distribution, gpu queue length, per-token timing traces | Detection: anomaly on per-token-time series vs baseline > 2x for 10m | Runbook: throttle long-context clients -> enable aggressive batching policy for best-effort -> open perf trace -> revert changes after stabilization | Automated action: smart-routing to lower-latency variant (quantized smaller model) for new requests while preserving pinned users. | Escalation: runtime -> platform eng for infra scaling. | Sprint template: runtime: build canary of adaptive-routing and metrics dashboard.

3) Quality (regression in eval-set pass-rate) | chat hallucination rate increase detected by evals | Owner: applied-ml/product | Signals: eval pass-rate drop, customer quality complaints, rerank score distribution | Detection: eval-suite daily delta < -5% and customer complaints > threshold | Runbook: roll forward to previous verified model, trigger evaluation harness, run human-in-the-loop review | Automated action: auto-roll-back to verified artifact if regression crosses threshold for 2 runs | Escalation: applied-ml -> product -> Customer success loop. | Sprint template: product: add gating pipeline to CI/CD to block auto-deploy with failing evals.
runbook_snippets:
- quick-check: 'kubectl get pods -n runtime | grep CrashLoop' then check model pool health with /admin/pools
- fallback-toggle: POST /admin/pools/{pool}/fallback?variant=quantized-v1 (idempotent)
- telemetry-playback: run synthetic requests from the synthetic-runner to reproduce latency/5xx
- incident-notify: use template in #sre-reliability-playground, fill in the impact, mitigation taken, next steps
automation_and_tests:
Planned automations:
- Canary test harness that replays 1% of production traffic to a canary pool every 6 hours (owner: platform eng)
- Auto rollback policy for eval regressions (owner: product CI)
- Synthetic-scheduled smoke for each route with SLA threshold (owner: solutions eng)

Test matrix to build: routing failover (unit + integration), KV-cache warm/cold scenarios, batch size variability stress, model-variant quality comparison.
timeline_and_milestones:
Week 0-2: align stakeholders, finalize detection queries, pick 3 pilot feature teams.
Week 3-6: implement canary harness + create runbook snippets and mapping.
Week 7-10: deploy automated fallback for availability + test in canary.
Week 11-14: add auto-rollback for eval regressions, integrate with CI gating.
Week 15+: measure metrics (time-to-detect, MTTR, customer-impact) and iterate.
risks_and_open_questions:
- Risk: feature teams will resist standardized runbooks if they perceive loss of control. Mitigation: make runbooks configurable templates.
- Open: how do we handle multi-tenant noisy neighbors on Dedicated pools? (need platform eng input)
- Risk: false positives from automated rollback on noisy evals. Mitigation: require two consecutive failing runs + manual review flag for high-impact models.
- Open: exact SLO thresholds for some composite user journeys (chat+search) — product to propose by 2026-11-20.
communication_and_rhythm: Weekly 30-min reliability sync (Wed 10:00 PST) for pilot teams. Monthly reliability demo for execs with 3 KPIs: detection lag, MTTR, runbook reuse rate. Slack channel: #reliability-orchestration for async discussion.
metrics_and_success_criteria: Primary metrics: detection lag (s), MTTR (minutes), % of incidents resolved by automated fallback, SLO burn rate trend. Success target: detection lag < 90s for availability spikes, MTTR reduced by 40% vs baseline, automated fallback resolves >= 50% of incidents in pilot.
